verdict.rationale: Fedora states it is free with no ads and that 'your desktop is your own', which speaks to the no-lock-in part of the story. Community reports confirm it installs and runs well on varied hardware: a Framework AMD laptop, a budget Lenovo laptop that 'just worked', an older VAIO, and home servers. Real hardware caveats remain: users report Nvidia driver pain, VirtualBox display glitches and freezes on low-end machines, and the docs give no hardware-compatibility or architecture-support statement beyond an aarch64 WSL build. Missing for 10: first-party hardware/architecture support documentation, smooth Nvidia GPU support, reliable behavior on low-end and VirtualBox setups.
